successCriteria.description: LeaveService implements ILeaveService (submit/approve/reject/cancel) and is exported from src/modules/leave/index.ts, with each operation computing n exactly once via the shared countLeaveDays helper (no inline day-count re-derivation anywhere in the service).

On APPROVE, the service enforces both sufficiency (n <= availableDays) and overlap (no intersecting APPROVED request for the same employee regardless of leave type, via findApprovedOverlapping) in the same code path, throwing InsufficientBalanceError / OverlapError respectively.
The balance fiscal year is derived from the request's startDate exactly once per operation (a request crossing 31 Dec is charged in full to its startDate's year, never split).

Every status change + balance counter change + audit write runs through the SAME unit-of-work client in ONE transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK owned by the service; the client is passed through to balance and audit services).
A Fastify controller + routes file exist for the leave module and the routes are registered in src/app.ts (alongside the existing uptimeRoutes registration), so the leave endpoints are reachable.
Every leave route enforces RBAC via a route-level guard (employee for submit/cancel of own requests; manager or hr_admin for approve/reject), never inline in the controller.

constraints: The leave module must import other modules only through their public entry points (index.ts barrels), never from internal files — per the module-boundary rule in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

All database access goes through repository interfaces (GP-001); the service/controller must not issue SQL or pool queries directly — the unit-of-work client is passed to repository/service methods as the optional LAST parameter.

Negative-guard logic lives ONLY in BalanceService (src/modules/balance/balance.service.ts) and must not be duplicated in the leave service; the leave service relies on balance service methods for counter transitions.
countLeaveDays is the ONLY day-count implementation (binding rule 1); the leave service must import it from src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts and never re-derive the count inline.
No test files are created in this sub-phase (tests are owned by Phase 4c); the implementation must compile and pass the mechanical build gate without them.

Strict TypeScript: no `any` (use `unknown` + type guards), strict null checks; all async errors are caught and mapped to the shared error contract ({ error, code }) — no unhandled promise rejections (GP-006).
outOfScope: src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts and src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts (owned by Phase 4a) — this sub-phase consumes them but does not create or modify them.
Unit/integration tests for the leave module (tests/unit/modules/leave/*) — owned by Phase 4c; do not create test files or gate on test coverage here.
Balance counter transition logic, negative guards, and remainingDays derivation — owned by BalanceService (Phase 2 part 2); the leave service must not reimplement them.
Notification fanout/background delivery semantics (BullMQ) — the leave service may call NotificationService.notify but must not implement delivery or queueing.

ambiguities.description: Whether the leave service should emit notifications (via NotificationService) inside the same transaction as the status/balance/audit writes, or after commit. The intent lists notification as a dependency but does not state transactional placement.
options: Notify inside the same transaction (client passed through)
Notify after COMMIT (fire-and-forget, outside the transaction)

ambiguities.description: How the service resolves the balance record for a request: the intent says derive the year from startDate but does not specify how the policyId/balanceId is located (e.g. via leaveTypeId -> policy -> balance, or a direct balance lookup).
options: Resolve policy from leaveTypeId then balance by employee+policy+year
Look up balance directly by employee+leaveType+year
Require balanceId to be supplied by the caller

ambiguities.description: Whether the controller/routes must enforce the minimumNoticeDays and requiresManagerApproval policy rules (binding rules mention them) or whether those are deferred to a later phase.
options: Defer policy-rule enforcement to a later phase

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle transitions are strictly SUBMITTED -> APPROVED | REJECTED, and SUBMITTED | APPROVED -> CANCELLED; approve/reject/cancel must reject requests not in the correct prior state (e.g. approving a non-SUBMITTED request is an error).

On APPROVE, approvedBy/approvedAt are set; on REJECT, rejectedBy/rejectedAt/rejectionReason are set; on CANCEL, cancelledBy/cancelledAt are set — each transition stamps its actor/timestamp fields and updates updatedAt.

Counter transitions follow the binding semantics: SUBMIT reserves pendingDays += n; APPROVE moves pendingDays -= n / usedDays += n; REJECT/CANCEL(pending) release pendingDays -= n; CANCEL(approved) restores usedDays -= n — all via BalanceService, never directly.

Every state-changing operation (submit/approve/reject/cancel) writes exactly one audit record with the matching action (SUBMIT/APPROVE/REJECT/CANCEL) and the request id as entityId, in the same transaction as the status change.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: employee (own request); actorId must equal the request's employeeId
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: invalid input -> ValidationError (400); unknown employee/leaveType/policy -> NotFoundError (404); insufficient balance -> InsufficientBalanceError (422)

interfaceConstraints.authRule: manager or hr_admin; no self-approval (actorId must not equal the request's employeeId)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: not found -> NotFoundError (404); wrong prior state -> ValidationError (400); insufficient balance -> InsufficientBalanceError (422); overlap -> OverlapError (422)
not found -> NotFoundError (404); wrong prior state -> ValidationError (400); missing rejectionReason -> ValidationError (400)
not found -> NotFoundError (404); wrong prior state (not SUBMITTED/APPROVED) -> ValidationError (400)

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service must call BalanceService.reserve/approve/reject/cancel with the day count n and the unit-of-work client, matching the exact method signatures (balanceId, days, [requestStatus], client?) declared in IBalanceService — do not reimplement counter math.
The service must call AuditService.record(input, client?) with the AuditLogInput shape (entityType/entityId/action/oldValues/newValues/performedBy) and pass the same unit-of-work client.
The service must call NotificationService.notify(input, client?) with the NotificationInput shape and honor its both-or-null relatedEntityType/relatedEntityId invariant.
The service must import countLeaveDays from the leave module and use it as the single day-count source; the returned value is endDate - startDate + 1 inclusive calendar days.
The service must use the shared error types (ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientBalanceError, OverlapError) and their statusCode/code contract rather than ad-hoc errors.

Routes must register against the Fastify instance in the same style as uptimeRoutes (async plugin function receiving fastify) and be registered in src/app.ts alongside the existing uptimeRoutes registration.

integrationPoints.why: Orchestrator delegates all counter transitions (reserve/approve/reject/cancel) and sufficiency derivation; negative guards live here only.
Every state-changing operation writes an audit record in the same transaction (GP-002).
Persistence of the LeaveRequest aggregate and the findApprovedOverlapping overlap query used at approval.
Source of the unit-of-work PoolClient for the single transaction spanning status + balance + audit writes.
Leave routes must be registered so endpoints are reachable.
